items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1961-02-16
items.q: I remember him and Pete on trumpet me and Paul in the drum section.

ctx.x: a regular soldier cap in a raincoat. I remember him and Pete on trumpet me and Paul in the drum section. There was a funeral we had in Algiers. That's right. I'm glad you mentioned that. That's the first job I played after I got out the show at the Navy. Sure is the truth. I told Paul I didn't have no drums and no parade drum like that. I know he had that little bass drum for you. We used to call it Pollyann. It marked on the side. I wouldn't play that funeral with him. He called me bass drum.
I was going to ask one thing about the position of the bass drum and the snare drum in the band on the street the bass drum is always over on your left.

items.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier Interview
items.q: he was on the St. Joseph night when he asked me do I want to join the P-Round band because he was leaving the band on two weeks' notice.

ctx.x: Yeah, the two rods and something.

Yeah, yeah, separated tumscrew rods. And then the later years, I went in from, let's see, it was 28, when I was working, John Robichauds, he had another dance orchestra. We used to play it, locally work around, you know, country club the same way, evening dances, night dances. It was like the Young Tuxedo Band. items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1972-01-19
items.q: Paul Barch wouldn't play in the band that time, got to play in 1930.

ctx.x: So Paul Barch wasn't doing that band anymore then? Who? Paul Barch was gone. Oh no, no. He was up in New York that time.

Paul Barch wouldn't play in the band that time, got to play in 1930. And then during that time when Joe Ruzon got hoisted, had like a B or something, he kind of hoisted his mouth, so we replaced him with this fellow Caesar Thornton. Yeah, yeah. Yeah, he's from St. Louis, and he came down here on the boat. Not too much with sax, but he was a good arranger.
